requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: The `interleave` statement specifies the interleaved occurrence and handling of the receiving events `done`, `killed`, `timeout`, `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch` and `check`.
requirements.original: The `interleave` statement allows to specify the interleaved occurrence and handling of receiving events including `done`, `killed`, `timeout`, `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch` and `check`.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: The `interleave` statement has the syntax `interleave [@nodefault] { { [] (TimeoutStatement | ReceiveStatement | TriggerStatement | GetCallStatement | CatchStatement | CheckStatement | GetReplyStatement | DoneStatement | KilledStatement) StatementBlock } }`.
requirements.original:
interleave [ @nodefault ] "{" 
     { "[]" ( TimeoutStatement |
          ReceiveStatement |
          TriggerStatement |
          GetCallStatement |
          CatchStatement |
          CheckStatement |
          GetReplyStatement |
          DoneStatement |
          KilledStatement ) StatementBlock
     } 
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: Each branch of an `interleave` statement SHALL start with a reception statement (`timeout`, `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `catch`, `check`, `getreply`, `done` or `killed`) followed by a statement block.
requirements.original:
interleave [ @nodefault ] "{" 
     { "[]" ( TimeoutStatement |
          ReceiveStatement |
          TriggerStatement |
          GetCallStatement |
          CatchStatement |
          CheckStatement |
          GetReplyStatement |
          DoneStatement |
          KilledStatement ) StatementBlock
     } 
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: Interleaved behaviour CAN always be replaced by an equivalent set of nested `alt` statements.
requirements.original: Interleaved behaviour can always be replaced by an equivalent set of nested alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.condition: a reception statement in an interleave statement is executed
requirements.canonical: Whenever a reception statement within an `interleave` statement is executed, the following non-reception statements ARE executed subsequently until the next reception statement is reached, a `break` statement is reached, or the interleaved sequence ends.
requirements.original: a) Whenever a reception statement is executed, the following non-reception statements are subsequently executed until the next reception statement is reached, a break statement is reached, or the interleaved sequence ends.

requirements.subject: ent:reception-statement
requirements.canonical: A reception statement IS a TTCN-3 statement that may occur in sets of alternatives, i.e. `receive`, `check`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch`, `done`, `killed` and `timeout`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Reception statements are TTCN-3 statements which may occur in sets of alternatives, i.e. `receive`, `check`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch`, `done`, `killed` and `timeout`.

requirements.subject: ent:non-reception-statement
requirements.canonical: A non-reception statement IS any other non-control-transfer statement that can be used within the `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: Non-reception statements denote all other non-control-transfer statements which can be used within the `interleave` statement.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: none of the alternatives of the interleave statement can be executed
requirements.canonical: If none of the alternatives of the `interleave` statement can be executed, the default mechanism IS invoked.
requirements.original: b) If none of the alternatives of the `interleave` statement can be executed, the default mechanism will be invoked.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the default mechanism is invoked from an interleave statement
requirements.canonical: When the default mechanism is invoked from an `interleave` statement, the actual snapshot IS used to evaluate the altsteps that have been activated as defaults before entering the `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: This means, according to the semantics of the default mechanism, the actual snapshot will be used to evaluate those altsteps that have been activated before entering the `interleave` statement.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.condition: the interleave statement contains the @nodefault modifier
requirements.canonical: If an `interleave` statement contains the `@nodefault` modifier, all active default alternatives ARE ignored for the execution of that `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: If the `interleave` statement contains the `@nodefault` modifier, all active default alternatives are ignored for the execution of this `interleave` statement.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: The complete semantics of the default mechanism within an `interleave` statement IS given by replacing the `interleave` statement by an equivalent set of nested `alt` statements.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The complete semantics of the default mechanism within an `interleave` statement is given by replacing the `interleave` statement by an equivalent set of nested alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.condition: the interleave statement contains the @nodefault modifier
requirements.canonical: An `interleave` statement with the `@nodefault` modifier IS equivalent to a set of replacement `alt` statements that all have the `@nodefault` modifier.
requirements.original: If the `interleave` statement contains the `@nodefault` modifier, it is equivalent with all replacement `alt` statement having the `@nodefault` modifier.

ambiguity.issue: 'all replacement alt statement having' mixes singular/plural; meaning is that every replacement alt statement carries @nodefault.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.canonical: The default mechanism applies to each of the replacement `alt` statements of an `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: The default mechanism applies for each of these alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: If no `break` statement was encountered, the evaluation of the `interleave` statement continues by taking the next snapshot.
requirements.original: c) The evaluation then continues by taking the next snapshot if no break statement was encountered.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of an `interleave` statement IS terminated if a `break` statement is executed.
requirements.original: d) The evaluation of the interleave statement is terminated if a break statement is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: An `interleave` statement SHALL NOT contain the control transfer statements `activate`, `deactivate`, `repeat`, any call of an altstep, or any direct or indirect call of a user-defined function that includes reception statements.
requirements.original: a) Control transfer statements activate, deactivate, repeat, all calls of altsteps and (direct and indirect) calls of user-defined functions, which include reception statements, shall not be present in interleave statements.

readings: An `interleave` statement SHALL NOT contain `activate`, `deactivate`, `repeat`, any altstep call, or any (direct or indirect) call of a user-defined function that includes reception statements.
An `interleave` statement SHALL NOT contain `activate`, `deactivate`, `repeat`, or calls of altsteps or user-defined functions where any of these include reception statements.
ambiguity.issue: The scope of the relative clause 'which include reception statements' is unclear (only functions, or also altsteps / all listed items); first reading chosen because altsteps always contain reception statements. Also 'activate' and 'deactivate' are operations, not control transfer statements.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: A branch of an `interleave` statement SHALL NOT be guarded by a Boolean expression, i.e. the `[ ]` SHALL always be empty.
requirements.original: b) In addition, it is not allowed to guard branches of an interleave statement with Boolean expressions (i.e. the '[ ]' shall always be empty).

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: An `interleave` statement SHALL NOT contain an `else` branch.
requirements.original: It is also not allowed to specify else branches in interleaved behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.condition: the interleave statement is used inside control behaviour
requirements.canonical: An `interleave` statement used inside control behaviour SHALL only contain `timeout` statements in the event parts of its alternatives.
requirements.original: c) An interleave used inside control behaviour shall only contain timeout statements in the event parts of the alternatives.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: The control transfer statements `for`, `while`, `do-while` and `goto` MAY be used within `interleave` statements under the conditions stated in 20.4 restriction d).
requirements.original: d) The restricted use of the control transfer statements for, while, do-while, and goto within interleave statements is allowed under the following conditions:

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.condition: the statement block does not contain reception statements
requirements.canonical: The loop statements `for`, `while` and `do-while` MAY be used within an `interleave` statement only in statement blocks that do not contain reception statements.
requirements.original: The loop statements for, while, and do-while can be used within statements blocks that do not contain reception statements.

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.canonical: A `for`, `while` or `do-while` statement SHALL NOT be used within an `interleave` statement in a statement block that contains reception statements.
requirements.original: The loop statements for, while, and do-while can be used within statements blocks that do not contain reception statements.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.condition: the statement blocks do not contain reception statements
requirements.canonical: A `goto` statement MAY be used within an `interleave` statement for jumps within statement blocks that do not contain reception statements.
requirements.original: The goto statement can be used for defining jumps with statements blocks that do not contain reception statements and for specifying jumps out of interleave statements.

readings: A `goto` statement MAY jump only between positions inside statement blocks that contain no reception statements.
A `goto` statement MAY be placed in a statement block without reception statements and jump to any label of the interleave statement.
ambiguity.issue: 'jumps with statements blocks' is garbled ('within'?); it is unclear whether the jump target must also lie in a block without reception statements. First reading chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A `goto` statement MAY be used to jump out of an `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: The goto statement can be used for defining jumps with statements blocks that do not contain reception statements and for specifying jumps out of interleave statements.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY be activated as a default.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows the activation of altsteps (see clause 16.2.1) as defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: Each test component stores its defaults, i.e. its activated altsteps, as an ordered list.
requirements.original: For each test component the defaults, i.e. activated altsteps, are stored as an ordered list.

requirements.subject: ent:list-of-defaults
requirements.canonical: The list of defaults IS ordered in reverse order of activation, i.e. the last activated default is the first element in the list.
requirements.original: The defaults are listed in the reversed order of their activation i.e. the last activated default is the first element in the list of active defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `activate` and `deactivate` operations operate on the list of defaults.
requirements.original: The TTCN-3 operations activate (see clause 20.5.2) and deactivate (see clause 20.5.3) operate on the list of defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.condition: the activate operation creates a new default
requirements.canonical: If an `activate` operation creates a new default, the new default IS inserted as the first element into the list of defaults.
requirements.original: If an activate operation creates a new default, it is inserted as the first element into the list.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.condition: the default was previously suspended and is re-activated
requirements.canonical: A re-activated default that was previously suspended retains its position in the list of defaults.
requirements.original: Re-activated defaults that were previously suspended retain their position in the list.

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `deactivate` operation either removes a default from the list of defaults or suspends it, in which case the default remains in the list but is temporarily inactive.
requirements.original: The deactivate operation either removes a default from the list or suspends it in which case the default remains in the list, but is temporarily inactive.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default in the list of defaults IS identified by a default reference generated as the result of the corresponding `activate` operation.
requirements.original: A default in the default list can be identified by means of default reference that is generated as a result of the corresponding activate operation.
